summary: A description of the UCSD Computer Center's FTP server, which required a valid user code and password because the center charged for its services. It lists the FTP commands it accepted, and notes that each transfer ran as a separately billed job on its B6700 computer. It follows the FTP of RFC 354 with noted exceptions.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC documents the UCSD Computer Center's FTP service. It explains login requirements, supported transfer options, file attributes, and commands the service did not implement.

questions: what was the ucsd-cc ftp server
how did early ftp servers handle billing
subtitle: Commands and restrictions in the UCSD Computer Center FTP service.

tldr.problem: The UCSD Computer Center needed to authenticate and account for users transferring files through its service.
tldr.mechanism: Users provide a user code and password; each transfer runs as a separate B6700 process and is accounted for separately.
tldr.outcome: The RFC documents supported FTP commands and local extensions, including file attributes for storage and tape transfers.

today: The unit metadata lists RFC 532's status as Unknown. The RFC documents a site-specific FTP implementation and its stated exceptions.

sections.title: Access and Accounting
sections.content:
The UCSD Computer Center required a valid user code and password before accepting further FTP commands. The RFC says each file transfer was handled by a separate process on the B6700 and was billed separately for processor, input/output, core, and any tape charges.

The service allowed files to be accessed or stored on disk or tape and followed RFC 354 except where the document notes differences.
sections.plainLanguage: Users had to log in before issuing transfer commands. Each file transfer ran as its own process and was accounted for separately.

sections.title: Supported Transfer Settings
sections.content:
The service accepts byte size 8 and stream mode S. It supports ASCII and Image types and both file and record structuring; record structuring is meaningful only with ASCII and stream mode.

The local ALLO form can specify B6700 file attributes. For tape storage, the RFC requires the attribute MYUSE=OUT and says users must arrange with operators to locate and mount the tape.
sections.plainLanguage: The server supports selected transfer settings rather than every possible value. Its special ALLO command can set local file attributes, including tape-related ones.

sections.title: Line Handling and Missing Commands
sections.content:
XLINE enables record structuring at the server without requiring the remote user's host to issue STRU R. For text transfers, the server adds CRLF on output and removes it when receiving text, according to the RFC.

APPE was not implemented at the time, and DELE, RNTO, and RNFR were also unavailable through this FTP service. The document directs users to TELNET and the LIBMAINT program for deletion or renaming.
sections.plainLanguage: XLINE handles line endings for text transfers. The RFC lists append, delete, and rename operations that were not then implemented through FTP.
